lead: Peloton Interactive / PTON — the founder exits, the comeback begins
smaller: AMC Entertainment / AMC — the meme cinema buys more screens
Bitcoin / BTC-USD — the stolen billions come home
Nvidia / NVDA — the deal died, the chip bulls cheered
why_lead: Peloton was the largest one-session equity mover on the card (37.27 USD, +25.28% on 2022-02-08; +33.01% over five sessions; now +8.44% over 20) and the 8 February catalyst is new and concrete: Foley stepping down with about 2,800 job cuts [[n0827]], [[n0828]], new CEO Barry McCarthy [[n0813]], [[n0826]], activist Blackwells pushing for more [[n0758]], plus mainstream attention (NYT 'What Is Peloton Worth?' [[n1192]], Wirecutter [[n1173]], Marketing Brew [[n1194]]). Relation to earlier retail notes: Peloton appeared only as a secondary item on 2022-02-07 (takeover lottery ticket, WSJ report) and 2022-02-08 (the +20.93% takeover pop); this promotion to lead is justified by newly published 8 February evidence of a different catalyst (management reset and cost cuts) rather than the takeover rumour, which is now only background. The 2022-02-01 to 2022-02-04 drafts did not cover Peloton. Independent review (chronology): the takeover headlines already used in the 2022-02-08 Peloton item (Wedbush's Apple case and CNBC's 'why a deal might not happen') were removed from this lead; only the BBC exploring-a-takeover report [[n0651]] remains as background, so the lead rests on the 8 February reset evidence.
why_smaller: AMC Entertainment: the meme-revival reflex with a new company catalyst — AMC +10.19% and GameStop +12.96% on 8 February, AMC's URW lease agreements and ArcLight acquisitions [[n0754]], [[n0753]], MarketWatch's meme-era tax-bill tally [[n0735]]. Relation to earlier notes: the 2022-02-01 lead was GameStop ('one year on, the faithful buy again'); this is a secondary item with a new AMC-specific catalyst, not a repeat of that lead.

Bitcoin: a different crypto narrative from the 2022-02-08 'crypto spring' lead — the Justice Department's $3.6 billion seizure [[n0807]] and the laundering charges [[n0955]] (8 February, known per timing), TMX crypto futures [[n0944]], scams [[n1797]] and the US Treasury study on NFT money-laundering risk [[n0953]]; card BTC 44,118.45 USD, +0.63% on the day and +18.74% over five days, DOGE -4.33%. This is the fourth straight edition with a crypto item (2022-02-04 Bitcoin, 2022-02-07 MicroStrategy, 2022-02-08 Bitcoin lead), so it stays secondary and every cited headline is newly published on 8 February; the 20-day-level break test used in the 2022-02-08 lead was replaced by the seizure-day price reaction as the test.

Nvidia: the chip-leverage narrative after the confirmed Arm termination ([[n0823]], [[n1950]], [[n0843]], [[n0788]]); NVDA +1.54% lagged SOXX +2.53% while MRVL rose 6.89% and SOXL 7.35%, and SOXL is still -22.33% over 20 sessions versus SOXX -6.30%; inflation-data focus [[n1348]] as the trigger. Distinct from the 2022-02-03 secondary item on AMD's beat-and-raise (an earnings story) and from the 2022-02-04 TQQQ item (daily-reset decay), whose leverage sermon is not repeated here.
